summary: Removed the 'optional / decide later' framing for codex-command-runner across Overview, Research Findings, Implementation Strategy (steps 2/3/4/6), Files to Create/Modify, In Scope, Risk Areas, Acceptance Criteria US-001 (criteria 1/2/3/5/6, with criterion 6 explicitly exercising the elevated path), and Open Questions; replaced the deferral with a source-code citation to runner_pipe.rs:43-44 and runner_client.rs:231 that puts both bins in-scope mandatorily.

Promoted the Cargo.toml version-bump-via-/publish-sandbox-patch step into Implementation Strategy as mandatory (citing the publish-npm.yml lines 32-46 tag-vs-version gate), replaced all -sandbox-test.N test-tag examples with v<NEW_VERSION> framing across Architecture/Scope/Implementation/Risk Areas/Acceptance Criteria/Open Questions, expanded the Technical Constraints CI bullet to document the gate, and reframed Open Questions §4 from 'operational detail' to 'not an open question — verification runs against the real release'.

Corrected the upstream-release-model citation in three places (Research Findings line 55+58, Files to Create/Modify section 2 spec, and the matching US-002 acceptance criterion) to accurately describe bwrap as a Rust workspace bin target built from the codex-bwrap crate via cargo build --bin bwrap (rust-release.yml:258-274), dropped the inaccurate 'externally sourced, not a Rust crate' framing, and re-framed codex-linux-sandbox as a separate upstream landlock+seccomp crate distinct from bwrap rather than a fork-specific replacement.

Added Windows-arm64 as a third platform expansion candidate in Part B section 3 (per-platform bin build, target-agnostic install.ps1, codex-win32-arm64 npm suffix, LLVM/xwin vs windows-11-arm toolchain note) and extended the matching acceptance criterion.
